audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for sea teaching, sower, mystery of the reign, Isaiah hearing/seeing, soils, lamp, measure, seed growing secretly, mustard seed, parables, and storm calming.

verses.restored: Again he began to teach beside the sea. A very great crowd gathered to him, so that he entered a boat and sat in the sea, and the whole crowd was beside the sea on the land.

familiar.text: And he began again to teach by the sea side: and there was gathered unto him a great multitude, so that he entered into a ship, and sat in the sea; and the whole multitude was by the sea on the land.

modern.text: Once again Jesus began to teach beside the sea, and such a large crowd gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat in it, while all the people crowded along the shore.

original.text: Καὶ πάλιν ἤρξατο διδάσκειν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν. καὶ ⸀συνάγεται πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλος ⸀πλεῖστος, ὥστε αὐτὸν ⸂εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα⸃ καθῆσθαι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ⸀ἦσαν.

verses.restored: He taught them many things in parables, and in his teaching he said to them:

familiar.text: And he taught them many things by parables, and said unto them in his doctrine,

modern.text: And He taught them many things in parables, and in His teaching He said,

original.text: καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς πολλά, καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: Listen. Look, the sower went out to sow.

familiar.text: Hearken; Behold, there went out a sower to sow:

modern.text: “Listen! A farmer went out to sow his seed.

original.text: Ἀκούετε. ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ ⸀σπείρων σπεῖραι.

verses.restored: As he sowed, some fell beside the way, and the birds came and devoured it.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as he sowed, some fell by the way side, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it up.

modern.text: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.

original.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ σπείρειν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἦλθεν τὰ πετεινὰ καὶ κατέφαγεν αὐτό.

verses.restored: Other seed fell on rocky ground where it did not have much soil, and immediately it sprang up because it had no depth of soil.

familiar.text: And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth:

modern.text: Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἄλλο⸃ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸ πετρῶδες ⸀ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς·

verses.restored: When the sun rose, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered.

familiar.text: But when the sun was up, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.

modern.text: But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.

original.text: ⸂καὶ ὅτε ἀνέτειλεν ὁ ἥλιος⸃ ⸀ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.

verses.restored: Other seed fell among thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it gave no fruit.

familiar.text: And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.

modern.text: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings, and they yielded no crop.

original.text: καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ συνέπνιξαν αὐτό, καὶ καρπὸν οὐκ ἔδωκεν.

verses.restored: Other seed fell into beautiful/good soil and gave fruit, coming up and increasing; it bore thirty, sixty, and a hundredfold.

familiar.text: And other fell on good ground, and did yield fruit that sprang up and increased; and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred.

modern.text: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprouted, grew up, and produced a crop—one bearing thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, and another a hundredfold.”

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἄλλα ἔπεσεν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν καλήν, καὶ ἐδίδου καρπὸν ἀναβαίνοντα καὶ ⸀αὐξανόμενα, καὶ ἔφερεν ⸂ἓν τριάκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἓν⸃ ἑκατόν.

verses.restored: He said, Whoever has ears to hear, let that one hear.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

modern.text: Then Jesus said, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.” The Purpose of Jesus’ Parables (Isaiah 6:1–13; Matthew 13:10–17; Luke 8:9–10)

original.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν· ⸂Ὃς ἔχει⸃ ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.

verses.restored: When he was alone, those around him with the twelve asked him about the parables.

familiar.text: And when he was alone, they that were about him with the twelve asked of him the parable.

modern.text: As soon as Jesus was alone with the Twelve and those around Him, they asked Him about the parable.

original.text: ⸂Καὶ ὅτε⸃ ἐγένετο κατὰ μόνας, ⸀ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ περὶ αὐτὸν σὺν τοῖς δώδεκα ⸂τὰς παραβολάς⸃.

verses.restored: He said to them, To you has been given the mystery of the reign of the Divine, but to those outside everything comes in parables,

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables:

modern.text: He replied, “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables,

original.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ὑμῖν ⸂τὸ μυστήριον δέδοται⸃ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ· ἐκείνοις δὲ τοῖς ἔξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὰ πάντα γίνεται,

verses.restored: so that seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they turn back and be released.

familiar.text: That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them.

modern.text: so that, ‘they may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.’ ” The Parable of the Sower Explained (Matthew 13:18–23; Luke 8:11–15)

original.text: ἵνα βλέποντες βλέπωσι καὶ μὴ ἴδωσιν, καὶ ἀκούοντες ἀκούωσι καὶ μὴ συνιῶσιν, μήποτε ἐπιστρέψωσιν καὶ ἀφεθῇ ⸀αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: He said to them, Do you not know this parable? Then how will you know all the parables?

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables?

modern.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand any of the parables?

original.text: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην, καὶ πῶς πάσας τὰς παραβολὰς γνώσεσθε;

verses.restored: The sower sows the word.

familiar.text: The sower soweth the word.

modern.text: The farmer sows the word.

original.text: ὁ σπείρων τὸν λόγον σπείρει.

verses.restored: These are the ones beside the way where the word is sown: when they hear, immediately the adversary comes and takes away the word sown in them.

familiar.text: And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.

modern.text: Some are like the seeds along the path, where the word is sown. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.

original.text: οὗτοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ὅπου σπείρεται ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν ⸀εὐθὺς ἔρχεται ὁ Σατανᾶς καὶ αἴρει τὸν λόγον τὸν ἐσπαρμένον ⸂εἰς αὐτούς⸃.

verses.restored: Likewise, these are the ones sown on rocky ground: when they hear the word, immediately they receive it with joy,

familiar.text: And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness;

modern.text: Some are like the seeds sown on rocky ground. They hear the word and at once receive it with joy.

original.text: καὶ οὗτοί εἰσιν ⸀ὁμοίως οἱ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπειρόμενοι, οἳ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν τὸν λόγον ⸀εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνουσιν αὐτόν,

verses.restored: but they have no root in themselves and are temporary. Then when pressure or persecution comes because of the word, immediately they stumble.

familiar.text: And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.

modern.text: But they themselves have no root, and they remain for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.

original.text: καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιροί εἰσιν, εἶτα γενομένης θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον ⸀εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζονται.

verses.restored: Others are the ones sown among thorns: these are those hearing the word,

familiar.text: And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word,

modern.text: Others are like the seeds sown among the thorns. They hear the word,

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἄλλοι εἰσὶν οἱ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπειρόμενοι· ⸂οὗτοί εἰσιν⸃ οἱ τὸν λόγον ⸀ἀκούσαντες,

verses.restored: but the worries of the age, the deceit of wealth, and desires for other things enter in and choke the word, and it becomes fruitless.

familiar.text: And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.

modern.text: but the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desire for other things come in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

original.text: καὶ αἱ μέριμναι τοῦ ⸀αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου καὶ αἱ περὶ τὰ λοιπὰ ἐπιθυμίαι εἰσπορευόμεναι συμπνίγουσιν τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.

verses.restored: Those sown on beautiful/good soil are the ones who hear the word, receive it, and bear fruit: thirty, sixty, and a hundredfold.

familiar.text: And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.

modern.text: Still others are like the seeds sown on good soil. They hear the word, receive it, and produce a crop—thirtyfold, sixtyfold, or a hundredfold.” The Lesson of the Lamp (Luke 8:16–18)

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἐκεῖνοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν σπαρέντες, οἵτινες ἀκούουσιν τὸν λόγον καὶ παραδέχονται καὶ καρποφοροῦσιν ⸂ἓν τριάκοντα καὶ ἓν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἓν⸃ ἑκατόν.

verses.restored: He said to them, Does the lamp come so that it may be placed under a basket or under a bed? Is it not to be placed on the lampstand?

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Is a candle brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick?

modern.text: Jesus also said to them, “Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed? Doesn’t he set it on a stand?

original.text: Καὶ ἔλεγεν ⸀αὐτοῖς· Μήτι ⸂ἔρχεται ὁ λύχνος⸃ ἵνα ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον τεθῇ ἢ ὑπὸ τὴν κλίνην, οὐχ ἵνα ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν ⸀τεθῇ;

verses.restored: For nothing is hidden except to be made visible, nor has anything become concealed except to come into the open.

familiar.text: For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither was any thing kept secret, but that it should come abroad.

modern.text: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be brought to light.

original.text: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ⸀κρυπτὸν ἐὰν μὴ ⸀ἵνα φανερωθῇ, οὐδὲ ἐγένετο ἀπόκρυφον ἀλλʼ ἵνα ⸂ἔλθῃ εἰς φανερόν⸃.

verses.restored: If anyone has ears to hear, let that one hear.

familiar.text: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

modern.text: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”

original.text: εἴ τις ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.

verses.restored: He said to them, Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you measure, it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Take heed what ye hear: with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given.

modern.text: He went on to say, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and even more will be added to you.

original.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Βλέπετε τί ἀκούετε. ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν καὶ προστεθήσεται ⸀ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: For whoever has, more will be given; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.

familiar.text: For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath.

modern.text: For whoever has will be given more. But whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” The Seed Growing Secretly

original.text: ὃς γὰρ ⸀ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ· καὶ ὃς οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ⸀ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He said, The reign of the Divine is like this: a person casts seed on the ground,

familiar.text: And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground;

modern.text: Jesus also said, “The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.

original.text: Καὶ ἔλεγεν· Οὕτως ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ⸀ὡς ἄνθρωπος βάλῃ τὸν σπόρον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

verses.restored: and sleeps and rises night and day, and the seed sprouts and lengthens; how, he does not know.

familiar.text: And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.

modern.text: Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.

original.text: καὶ καθεύδῃ καὶ ἐγείρηται νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν, καὶ ὁ σπόρος ⸀βλαστᾷ καὶ μηκύνηται ὡς οὐκ οἶδεν αὐτός.

verses.restored: The earth bears fruit by itself: first blade, then head, then full grain in the head.

familiar.text: For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.

modern.text: All by itself the earth produces a crop—first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.

original.text: ⸀αὐτομάτη ἡ γῆ καρποφορεῖ, πρῶτον χόρτον, ⸂εἶτα στάχυν, εἶτα⸃ ⸂πλήρης σῖτον⸃ ἐν τῷ στάχυϊ.

verses.restored: When the fruit is ready, immediately he sends the sickle, because the harvest has come.

familiar.text: But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.

modern.text: And as soon as the grain is ripe, he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come. ” The Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13:31–32; Luke 13:18–19)

original.text: ὅταν δὲ ⸀παραδοῖ ὁ καρπός, ⸀εὐθὺς ἀποστέλλει τὸ δρέπανον, ὅτι παρέστηκεν ὁ θερισμός.

verses.restored: He said, How shall we compare the reign of the Divine, or in what parable shall we set it?

familiar.text: And he said, Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?

modern.text: Then He asked, “To what can we compare the kingdom of God? With what parable shall we present it?

original.text: Καὶ ἔλεγεν· ⸀Πῶς ὁμοιώσωμεν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἢ ἐν ⸀τίνι ⸂αὐτὴν παραβολῇ θῶμεν⸃;

verses.restored: It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown on the ground, is smaller than all the seeds on the earth.

familiar.text: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is less than all the seeds that be in the earth:

modern.text: It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.

original.text: ὡς ⸀κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃς ὅταν σπαρῇ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ⸂μικρότερον ὂν⸃ πάντων τῶν ⸀σπερμάτων τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς—

verses.restored: Yet when it is sown, it grows up and becomes greater than all the garden plants and makes great branches, so that the birds of the heavens can nest under its shade.

familiar.text: But when it is sown, it groweth up, and becometh greater than all herbs, and shooteth out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under the shadow of it.

modern.text: But after it is planted, it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches, so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.”

original.text: καὶ ὅταν σπαρῇ, ἀναβαίνει καὶ γίνεται ⸂μεῖζον πάντων τῶν λαχάνων⸃ καὶ ποιεῖ κλάδους μεγάλους, ὥστε δύνασθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σκιὰν αὐτοῦ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνοῦν.

verses.restored: With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear.

familiar.text: And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it.

modern.text: With many such parables Jesus spoke the word to them, to the extent that they could understand.

original.text: Καὶ τοιαύταις παραβολαῖς πολλαῖς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον, καθὼς ἠδύναντο ἀκούειν·

verses.restored: He did not speak to them without a parable, but privately to his own disciples he explained all things.

familiar.text: But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.

modern.text: He did not tell them anything without using a parable. But privately He explained everything to His own disciples. Jesus Calms the Storm (Psalms 107:1–43; Matthew 8:23–27; Luke 8:22–25)

original.text: χωρὶς δὲ παραβολῆς οὐκ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς, κατʼ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς ⸂ἰδίοις μαθηταῖς⸃ ἐπέλυεν πάντα.

verses.restored: On that day, when evening came, he said to them, Let us pass over to the other side.

familiar.text: And the same day, when the even was come, he saith unto them, Let us pass over unto the other side.

modern.text: When that evening came, He said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side.”

original.text: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὀψίας γενομένης· Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν.

verses.restored: Leaving the crowd, they took him along as he was in the boat, and other boats were with him.

familiar.text: And when they had sent away the multitude, they took him even as he was in the ship. And there were also with him other little ships.

modern.text: After they had dismissed the crowd, they took Jesus with them, since He was already in the boat. And there were other boats with Him.

original.text: καὶ ἀφέντες τὸν ὄχλον παραλαμβάνουσιν αὐτὸν ὡς ἦν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ, καὶ ἄλλα ⸀πλοῖα ἦν μετʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: A great windstorm arose, and the waves were throwing themselves into the boat, so that the boat was already filling.

familiar.text: And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full.

modern.text: Soon a violent windstorm came up, and the waves were breaking over the boat, so that it was being swamped.

original.text: καὶ γίνεται λαῖλαψ ⸂μεγάλη ἀνέμου⸃, ⸂καὶ τὰ⸃ κύματα ἐπέβαλλεν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, ὥστε ⸂ἤδη γεμίζεσθαι τὸ πλοῖον⸃.

verses.restored: He was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. They woke him and said to him, Teacher, does it not matter to you that we are perishing?

familiar.text: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?

modern.text: But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. So they woke Him and said, “Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?”

original.text: καὶ ⸂αὐτὸς ἦν⸃ ⸀ἐν τῇ πρύμνῃ ἐπὶ τὸ προσκεφάλαιον καθεύδων· καὶ ⸀ἐγείρουσιν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διδάσκαλε, οὐ μέλει σοι ὅτι ἀπολλύμεθα;

verses.restored: He woke, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, Be silent; be still. The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

familiar.text: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

modern.text: Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea. “Silence!” He commanded. “Be still!” And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.

original.text: καὶ διεγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ ἀνέμῳ καὶ εἶπεν τῇ θαλάσσῃ· Σιώπα, πεφίμωσο. καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη μεγάλη.

verses.restored: He said to them, Why are you fearful? Do you not yet have trust?

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?

modern.text: “Why are you so afraid?” He asked. “Do you still have no faith?”

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τί δειλοί ἐστε; ⸀οὔπω ἔχετε πίστιν;

verses.restored: They feared a great fear and said to one another, Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

familiar.text: And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

modern.text: Overwhelmed with fear, they asked one another, “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?”

original.text: καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν φόβον μέγαν, καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Τίς ἄρα οὗτός ἐστιν ὅτι καὶ ὁ ἄνεμος καὶ ἡ θάλασσα ⸀ὑπακούει αὐτῷ;
